newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Fergie admits she unfit to be a royal.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Fergie admits she unfit to be a royal.

text.p: The Duchess of York, popularly known as Fergie, was quoted on Monday as describing herself as a "national disgrace".

British newspapers, reporting what they said were extracts of her autobiography being published later his month, quoted the 36-year-old duchess as saying; "I was never cut out for the job. I was unsuitable, always had been."

Fergie (Sarah Ferguson), who was divorced from Queen Elizabeth's second son Prince Andrew earlier this year, appeared to acknowledge the shame of pictures in 1992 showing her frolicking topless with her American lover and business adviser John Bryan.
"I was exposed for what I truly was. Worthless, unfit, a national disgrace," several newspapers quoted her as writing.
"I was hopeless from the start, the wrong person in the wrong place at the wrong time. They could never make me the perfect princess," she adds.
The pictures were shown in newspapers around the world at a time when Fergie was spending a holiday with the queen and other senior members of the royal family.

She reportedly got through a difficult meeting with the queen thanks to glasses of brandy, half a Valium tablet and the support of her husband. The couple were married in 1986 and have two young daughters.
Fergie's book "My Story" is to be published in mid-November by New York-based publishers Simon and Schuster. Hello magazine will be publishing extracts this week in Britain.
It coincides with an unflattering book about her written by Allan Starkie, a friend of Bryan, which the duchess failed last month to have banned.
Fergie flaunted royal convention again this week by endorsing a product for an advertisement. She is pictured brandishing a new Olympus digital camera while passing New York's Statue of Liberty.
The advertisement will appear in continental Europe but not in Britain in a bid to save the her former royal in-laws from embarrassment.
"This is a matter entirely for the duchess. Her financial affairs are her own," a spokesman for Buckingham Palace said.
The duchess, who is reported to have huge debts, is said to have been paid some 20,000 pounds ($30,000) for the advertisement.
